title: Creative One & Two Button Games
author: acrolicious
selftext:
Hello Everyone!

I posted a while back about using AI to create an accessible tool and game hub for my brother, Ben, who relies on right and left head movements for all input.

For context: Ben has Tubb4a-related Leukodystrophy (H-ABC), a progressive condition that caused him to lose the ability to walk, talk, and use his hands. Eye-tracking doesn't work for him, and he lacks the fine motor control needed for standard head-tracking or mouth switches. He can only turn his head left or right—and eventually, may only have a single input direction.

I made it my mission to give him as much independence and entertainment as possible.

Over the last year, we’ve built him a whole suite of custom tools:

Custom Media & Tools: A streaming app, custom YouTube search, Google Assistant integration, a phrase board, and a real-time conversation app.

3D & Interactive Games: As AI models have advanced, we’ve upgraded from simple board games to fully interactive Three.js-based 3D games—all controlled entirely with 1 or 2 inputs.

Because these types of dedicated, low-input tools and games are so rare, we wanted to make sure other families could use them too.

Everything we build is 100% free, open-source, and requires no login:

Tools & Hub: https://www.bennyshub.com

Games: https://www.switchedgames.org

This is all made possible through our non-profit! Beyond the software, we also donate free adaptive switch kits (just like the set Ben uses) to anyone who applies.

We’d love for you to check out the sites, share them with anyone who might benefit, or drop any feedback/ideas in the comments!

comments.author: jbartorii
comments.body:
I just published a free-to-play, casual shotgun FPS where you really only need the mouse/left-click to blow stuff up. Not sure if that's accessible enough for his needs, but thought I'd share in the event it is.

[https://fun.johnbrodish.com/street-sweeper/](https://fun.johnbrodish.com/street-sweeper/) 

I'd be happy to refine controls if needed as this is just a fun weekend project for me.

replies.author: acrolicious
replies.body:
Ben is unable to control directions with a traditional mouse, however, we have figure out a way for him to at least control left and right movements with a racing style game. 

Not sure if your game would work for him but we are always willing to look at and adapt games if they fit for our hub if that's something you're interested in. 

Take a look at what I mean:

https://narbehouse.github.io/bennyshub/apps/games/BENNYSRACETRACKS/index.html

replies.author: jbartorii
replies.body:
Hmmm. I'm using a trackpad where I just gently move my finger and tap in my game. I see what you mean though.

Giving me ideas for something like the shooting gallery in ocarina of time, where maybe targets move in front of the reticule and you just press space at the right time to shoot them

replies.author: acrolicious
replies.body: Could work for the library. It's a good idea. It probably wouldn't be something Ben could play unless the target duration was extremely forgiving to give adequate time to hit 🤔

replies.author: jbartorii
replies.body: I might spin up a version of the game that could work for benny, will let ya know

comments.author: Warsel77
comments.body:
Hey, this is awesome.  
Are these left & right head movements binary or is graduation possible?

replies.author: acrolicious
replies.body: Binary right and left head movements (Ben doesn't have the fine motor control) but he can do short and long presses to give him a total of 4 inputs.
